text:
pradeep: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — recurring CPU spike alerts are still noisy. Want a concrete playbook to reduce churn and assign owners. Goal: fewer wakeups, clearer SLO->paging mapping.
jamie: +1. I can sketch a dedupe window and ownership model. Is this only the nightly batch or other signals too? :thinking_face: 
sara: Nightly batch is the big one, but we also saw duplicate infra alerts during canary rollouts. Two separate sources.
alex: For dedupe, we should prefer a request-scoped dedupe (same resource within 10m) + global flood protection. Example rule: `if count(alerts where host==host and metric==cpu) > 3 within 10m then suppress duplicates`.
pradeep: That sounds good. Also want to adjust threshold for the infra CPU alarm from 85% -> 90% for non-prod fleets, keep 80% for prod. Can we make thresholds config-per-fleet?
jamie: Yes, config-per-fleet is already in the alerting backend. I'll add `fleet_thresholds` to the rule schema. Will post a PR with the change. ETA: EOD Thurs.
sara: Paging policy proposal: only page on severity=sev1 or if alert_count_for_service > 5 in 5m. Sev2 should create a ticket and notify #oncall but not wake up. Thoughts?
alex: Agree with not paging on isolated sev2s. For the >5 flood rule we should make it parametric per-service (high-availability services get lower flood trigger).
pradeep: Action items I'll track: 1) jamie: PR to add fleet_thresholds + example config (due Thurs EOD) 2) alex: implement dedupe/suppression prototype and post logs snippet (due next Tue) 3) sara: update paging playbook section + test checklist (due next Wed) 4) ops: add runbook link to alert template (who is ops on this thread?)
jamie: I'll own the PR and coordinate with eng-platform for rollout. Tagging deploy-bot for validation.
deploy-bot: [automated] linked CI: https://ci.internal/runs/4321 — alert-schema tests passed on staging :white_check_mark:
alex: Prototype logic I'll drop in `infra/alerting/suppressors` and include a small unit test showing dedupe window. Example snippet I plan to use:
```
# suppressors/dedupe.py
class HostDedupe:
    window_secs = 600
    def should_suppress(alerts):
        # group by (host, metric)
        return grouped_count > threshold
```

sara: For ownership, propose adding `remediation_owner` tag to every alert which maps to oncall schedule. That way paging decisions can be automated. I'll update playbook to require this field for sev1/2.
pradeep: Good. Also we discovered recurring pattern: nightly batch + a long-tail memory leak together cause repeated alerts overnight. We should add a recurring incident monitor: weekly summary of top-10 noisy rules and owners. Can someone take the weekly report?
jamie: I can add a scheduled job that generates the weekly noisy-rule report and posts to #eng-oncall on Mondays. ETA: next Monday dry-run.
pradeep: Perfect. Let's keep scope tight: first roll out dedupe + fleet thresholds + paging changes to staging for 2 weeks, monitor noise reduction metric (alerts_per_service_per_day). If reduction > 40% on staging, plan prod rollout.
alex: I'll instrument `alerts_per_service_per_day` at ingestion and add a Grafana panel.
pradeep: Summary of decisions: dedupe window per-host (10m) + flood protection, fleet-specific thresholds, page only sev1 or flood > parametric threshold, add `remediation_owner` tag, weekly noisy-rule report. Owners & due dates listed above. I'll add these to the postmortem follow-up doc and mark as blockers for the next oncall rotation if not done. :white_check_mark:
sara: I'll update the playbook and link the runbook PR here when ready.
jamie: PR opened: https://repo.internal/alerts/pulls/128 — please review.
alex: Dropped initial suppressor prototype: https://repo.internal/alerts/commit/abc123 — tests included.
pradeep: Thanks all. We'll reconvene next Wed for a short check-in (15m) to ensure staging metrics look good. :calendar:
